name: 7.2 A Single Population Mean using the Student t Distribution
_note: Built 2026-08-12. Two reuses (q4-ci-mean-t, q6-ci-mean-t-story - both health=ok, never filed) plus eight authored (q14-degrees-of-freedom, q15-t-vs-z, q16-t-critical-value, q17-t-interval-mean, q18-t-interval-interpret, q19-raw-data-to-interval, q20-t-width-dials, pre-frq-grade-a-t-interval) = ten. Points 10+10+10+10+10+10+10+9+9+12 = 100. BookSHelf 7.2 is the confidence interval for a population mean when sigma is unknown: the Student t-distribution, degrees of freedom n-1, the t-score, EBM = t_(alpha/2)*s/sqrt(n), the interval, and the interpretation. Pre-FRQ mirrors frq/inference-for-means/q3-single-mean-interpreting-confidence-interval.php; dropped category is ASSESSING THE CLAIM (the mirror's third rubric line - a plausible answer interprets the interval and explains the confidence level without ever checking whether a claimed value falls inside it). This is deliberately DIFFERENT from 7.1's pre-FRQ drop (Confidence Level Meaning) - the two pre-FRQs must not teach the same lesson.
